set: A: one sheet across each of the ten beats, with no time and no word on it

issues.where: machine reveal, frames 2–12, right-hand return lane
issues.what: The glass ball can be tracked intermittently, but its internal arrow gets lost among the reflections and rings. The lane carries a pinball; there is no readable character pose for most of the sheet.
issues.fix: Keep the wide reveal, but cut in on the ball for a held bracing pose and put a dark surface behind the white arrow so it survives the glass reflections.

issues.what: The moving ball and flippers sell the hits, but the internal arrow mostly spins or blurs. There is no readable prepare, compress, and recover sequence on an individual hit.
issues.fix: Feature one hit: aim the tip away from the approaching flipper, squash the arrow across the impact axis, then stretch and briefly hold a clean recoil silhouette.

issues.where: Coffee release and playfield cut, frames 4–6
issues.what: The extra round forms and glare make it hard to follow which ball contains the character precisely when it should react to the swarm.
issues.fix: Give the cursor a distinct recoil before the cut and keep a dark backing behind its white silhouette while the extra balls scatter.

issues.what: The bare arrow moves much like a normal pointer until it goes into the intake. The suction and capsule change are clear, but there is little readable anticipation or recoil as it loses control.
issues.fix: Hold a tilted-back hesitation outside the mouth, then pull the tip sharply toward the intake and let the arrow recoil against the glass once sealed.

issues.what: The tight views have a legible arrow, but most of the change is rotation with the ball; the turn from directed travel to being pulled into the funnel has no distinct bracing pose.
issues.fix: At the rail lip, counter-lean the tip against the turn for a beat, then widen it on the first hard change of direction before releasing into the spiral.

issues.what: did not read: the travel from the tube into the machine is read; that the page's light goes down to dusk, the marquee lights and the three tiers light in a wave, lamp by lamp, until the whole machine stands in the frame is not: the read is of a ball carried along, with no feeling and no event.
issues.fix: The wave as an event of its own: the page's light going down, the marquee coming on first, then each tier's lamps in order from the top, and the pull back ending on the whole machine held long enough to be taken in.

issues.what: did not read: the hope at the Corporate HQ doors is read; that the doors slam, that the ball hits them and that the arrow is pressed flat against the inside of the glass is not: the read goes from hopeful to being sent down to the next field.
issues.fix: The slam and the flattening seen close: the doors shutting in one or two frames, the ball on them, the arrow flat on the inside of the glass and held there before it slides back down the carpet.

issues.what: did not read: the battering is read; that the three coffee bumpers rattle the ball between them and that the arrow is thrown flat on each hit is not: the read has flippers batting it and says that the single reactions are hard to read.
issues.fix: Each bumper hit answered by the arrow in the ball: thrown against the far wall and flat for a few frames, at a size in the picture at which it can be seen, with the three cups as what does it.

issues.what: did not read: that balls like it spill out is read; that it lands in the inbox, that the steel balls chase it and hit it and that the whole tier strobes is not: the read has it seat itself at the coffee station and spring away.
issues.fix: The inbox readable as an inbox where the ball lands, the steel balls seen to chase and to strike it, each strike answered inside the ball, and the strobe of the tier on those frames.

issues.what: did not read: the read is of a woozy, battered arrow that crumples at the right flipper and is knocked across the field again. The fall toward the gap, the catch at the last instant and the sag of relief are not in the read.
issues.fix: The fall toward the gap as its own moment, the catch at the last instant, and the sag of relief held inside the ball in the slow motion the beat has.

reads.read: Tentatively curious, then startled and trapped: the cursor approaches the round intake, is sealed in a clear ball and drops down the tube.
Trapped and being carried along, with no further feeling I can distinguish: the ball goes from the intake tube into the machine’s right-hand lane.
Nervously bracing: the ball pauses at the launcher, then shoots up the lane and into the playfield.
Intent and perhaps hopeful: after rolling among the bumpers, the arrow pitches up toward the Corporate HQ doors, then is sent down to the next field.
Buffeted and scrambling: the ball drops past the office bumpers and gets batted back and forth by the flippers; the individual reactions are hard to read.
Caught off guard: the ball seats itself at the Coffee station, then springs away as several lookalike balls spill out and it drops to the next level.
Stunned and bracing again: the ball lands at You’re Fired, the arrow pancakes and springs back upright, then gets thrown back into play.
Determined at first, then out of control: the ball gets onto the raised wire track, the arrow flips at the far end, and the ball circles the funnel.
Woozy and battered: the ball comes out of the funnel and the arrow crumples at the right flipper before getting knocked across the field again.
Worn out, then ready to move on: the ball drains, the arrow comes out bare at Assessment Complete, and after a short pause it clicks Continue.
